title: C.N.A FT Nights
description:
ooking for a FT C.N.A to join our team. 12-hour shift.

Purpose of Your Job Position

The primary purpose of your job position is to provide each patient with routine daily nursing care and services in accordance with the patient's assessment and care plan, and as may be directed by your supervisors.

Delegation of Authority

As a Certified Nursing Assistant, you are delegated the administrative authority, responsibility, and accountability necessary for carrying out your assigned duties.

Job Functions

Every effort has been made to identify the essential functions of this position. However, it in no way states or implies that these are the only duties you will be required to perform. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or is an essential function of the position.

Duties and Responsibilities

Administrative Functions

 Record all entries are informative and descriptive manner.

 Use only authorized abbreviations established by this facility when recording information.

 Report all changes in the patients to the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse as soon as practical.

 Report all accidents and incidents you observe on the shift that they occur.

Admission, Transfer, and Discharge Functions

 Ensure that the patient's room is ready for receiving the patient (i.e., bed made, name tags up, admission kit available, etc.).

 Greet patient and escort them to their room.

Personnel Functions

 Perform all assigned tasks in accordance with our established policies and procedures, and as instructed by your supervisors.

 Follow work assignments, and/or work schedules in completing and performing your assigned tasks.

 Cooperate with inter-departmental personnel, as well as other facility personnel to ensure that nursing services can be adequately maintained to meet the needs of the residents.

 Create and maintain an atmosphere of warmth, personal interest and positive emphasis, as well as a calm environment throughout the unit and shift.

 Meet with your shift’s nursing personnel, on a regularly scheduled basis, to assist in identifying and correcting problem areas, and/or the improvement of services.

 Report all complaints and grievances made by the resident.

 Notify the facility when you will be late or absent from work.

 Report occupational exposures to blood, body fluids, infectious materials, and hazardous chemicals to your supervisor.

Personal Nursing Care Functions

 Participate in and receive the nursing report upon reporting for duty.

 Follow established policies concerning exposure to blood/body fluids.

 Assist patients with daily dental and mouth care (i.e., brushing teeth/dentures, oral hygiene, special mouth care, etc.).

 Assist patients with bath functions (i.e., bedbath, tub or shower bath, etc.) as directed.

 Assist patients with ADLs necessary.

 Keep patients dry (i.e., change gown, clothing, linen, etc., when it becomes wet or soiled).

 Change bed linens, make beds. Keep linens tight to avoid wrinkles from forming under the patients.

 Put extra covers on beds as requested.

 Maintain intake and output records as instructed.

 Assist patients in preparing for medical tests (i.e., lab work, x-ray, therapy, dental, etc.).

 Assist patients in preparing for activity and social programs (i.e., church services, parties, visitors, etc.).

 Assist in transporting patients to/from appointments, activity and social programs, etc., as necessary.

 Assist with lifting, turning, moving, positioning, and transporting patients into and out of beds, chairs, bathtubs, wheelchairs, lifts etc.

 Assist patients to walk with or without self-help devices as instructed.

 Perform restorative and rehabilitative procedures as instructed.

 Change dressings, bandages, binders, etc., as instructed.

 Weigh and measure patients as instructed.

 Measure and record temperatures, pulse, and respirations (TPRs) as instructed.

 Answer calls promptly.

 Ensure that patients who are unable to call for help are checked frequently.

 Check each patientes routinely to ensure that his/her personal care needs are being met in accordance with his/her wishes.

Special Nursing Care Functions

 Observe and report the presence of pressure areas and skin breakdowns to prevent decubitus ulcers (bedsores).

 Report injuries of an unknown source, including skin tears.

 Assist with the application of slings, elastic bandages, binders, etc.

 Turn all medications found in the resident’s room/possession over to the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse.

 Watch for and report any change in room temperature, ventilation, lighting, etc.

Food Service Functions

 Prepare patients for meals (i.e., take to bathroom, wash hands, comb hair, raise bed, position tables, place bibs, take to/from dining room, etc.).

 Serve food trays. Assist with feeding as indicated (i.e., cutting foods, feeding, assist in dining room supervision, etc.).

 Assist patients with identifying food arrangements (i.e., informing patient with sight problem of foods that are on his/her tray, where it is located, if it is hot/cold, etc.).

 Record the patients food/fluid intake. Report changes in the patient’s eating habits.

 Keep patient’s water pitchers clean and filled with fresh water (on each shift) and within easy reach

 Perform after meal care (i.e., remove trays, clean hands, face, clothing, take to bathroom, brush teeth, clean dentures, etc.).

 Check rooms for food articles (i.e., food in proper container, unauthorized food items, etc.).

Staff Development

 Attend and participate in scheduled training and educational classes to maintain current certification as a Nursing Assistant.

 Attend and participate in scheduled orientation programs and activities.

 Attend and participate in annual OSHA and CDC in-service training programs for hazard communication, TB management, and bloodborne pathogens standard.

 Attend and participate in advance directive in-service training programs as scheduled.

 Maintain Relias learning

Safety and Sanitation

 Participate in appropriate in-service training programs prior to performing tasks that involve potential exposure to blood/body fluids.

 Wash hands before and after performing any service

 Keep the nurses’ call system within easy reach

 Immediately notify the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse of elopement

 Follow established safety precautions in the performance of all duties.

 Keep patient’s personal possessions off the floor and properly stored.

 Keep floors dry. Report spills immediately.

 Keep excess supplies and equipment off the floor. Store in designated areas.

 Wash wheelchairs, walkers, etc., as instructed.

 Clean, disinfect, and return all patient care equipment to its designated storage area after each use.

 Perform routine housekeeping duties (i.e., clean bedrails, overbed table, night stand, etc., that relate to nursing care procedures).

 Before leaving work area for breaks, or at the end of the work day, store all tools, equipment, and supplies.

 Report all hazardous conditions and equipment to the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse immediately.

 Report all safety violations.

 Follow established smoking regulations. Report all violations.

 Report any communicable or infectious disease to the Director of Nursing Services and/or to the Infection Control Coordinator.

 Follow established isolation precautions and procedures.

 Follow established procedures in the use and disposal of personal protective equipment.

 Wear and/or use safety equipment and supplies (e.g., back brace, mechanical lifts, etc.) when lifting or moving residents.

 Report missing/illegible labels and SDSs to your supervisor.

Equipment and Supply Functions

 Use only the equipment you have been trained to use.

 Operate all the equipment in a safe manner.

 Use only the equipment and supplies necessary to do the job. Do not be wasteful.

 Report defective equipment to the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse.

 Inform the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse of your equipment and supply needs.

Care Plan Functions

 Review care plans daily to determine if changes in the resident’s daily care routine have been made on the care plan.

 Inform the nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse of any changes in the patient’s condition so that appropriate information can be entered on the care plan.

 Ensure that your notes reflect that the care plan is being followed.

Resident Rights

 Maintain the confidentiality of all patient care information.

 Ensure that you treat all patients fairly, and with kindness, dignity, and respect.

 Ensure that all nursing care is provided in privacy.

 Knock before entering the patient’s room.

 Report all grievances and complaints made by the patient to the Nurse Supervisor/Charge Nurse.

 Report all allegations of resident abuse and/or misappropriation of resident property.

 Honor the patient’s refusal of treatment request. Report such requests to your supervisor.

Working Conditions

 Works throughout the nursing service area (i.e., drug rooms, nurses’ stations, resident rooms, etc.).

 Moves intermittently during working hours.

 Is subject to frequent interruptions.

 Is involved with patient, personnel, visitors, government agencies/personnel, etc., under all conditions and circumstances.

 Is subject to hostile and emotionally upset residents, family members, personnel, and visitors.

 Communicates with nursing personnel and other department personnel.

 Works beyond normal working hours, on weekends and holidays, and in other positions temporarily, when necessary.

 Is subject to call-back during emergency conditions (e.g., severe weather, evacuation, post-disaster, etc.).

 Attends and participates in continuing educational programs.

 Is subject to injury from falls, burns from equipment, odors, etc., throughout the work day, as well as to reactions from dust, disinfectants, tobacco smoke, and other air contaminants.

 Is subject to exposure to infectious waste, diseases, conditions, etc., including TB and the AIDS and Hepatitis B viruses.

 May be subject to the handling of and exposure to hazardous chemicals.

Experience

Must be a licensed Certified Nursing Assistant in accordance with laws of this state.

Specific Requirements

 Must be able to read, write, speak and understand the English language.

 Must possess the ability to make independent decisions when circumstances warrant such action.

 Must possess the ability to deal tactfully with personnel, residents, family members, visitors, government agencies/personnel, and the general public.

 Must possess the ability and willingness to work harmoniously with other personnel.

 Must have patience, tact, a cheerful disposition and enthusiasm, as well as the willingness to handle difficult residents.

 Must be willing to seek out new methods and principles and be willing to incorporate them into existing nursing practices.

 Must be able to relate information concerning a resident’s condition.

 Must not pose a direct threat to the health and safety of other individuals in the workplace.

Physical and Sensory Requirements

 Must be able to move intermittently throughout the work day.

 Must be able to speak and write the English language in an understandable manner.

 Must be able to cope with the mental and emotional stress of the position.

 Must be able to see and hear or use prosthetics that will enable these senses to function adequately to ensure that the requirements of this position can be fully met.

 Must function independently and have flexibility, personal integrity, and the ability to work effectively with residents, personnel, and support agencies.

 Must meet the general health requirements set forth by the policies of this facility which include a medical and physical examination.

 Must be able to relate to and work with the ill, disabled, elderly, emotionally upset, and, at times, hostile people within the facility.

 Must be able to lift up to 10 pounds. Requires lifting more weight up to 100 pounds with assistance. Occasional pushing of carts and wheelchairs.

 May be necessary to assist in the evacuation of residents during emergency situations.

title: MAC Appeals Specialist
location: Polaris Pharmacy Services of Ft Lauderdale - Ft. Lauderdale, FL 33309
description:
WHO WE ARE
At Polaris Pharmacy Services, we’re more than a pharmacy — we’re a dedicated partner in care, transforming how patients experience long-term, post-acute, correctional, PACE, and specialty pharmacy services. As industry leaders, we’re raising the bar for quality and coordination across all sites of care, ensuring every patient receives seamless, compassionate, and expert support.

Our team thrives in a mission-driven environment where innovation meets purpose, and every role contributes to making a real impact. We offer more than just a job — we provide competitive pay, robust benefits, and genuine opportunities for career advancement.

If you're passionate about shaping the future of pharmacy and making a difference in the lives of those who need it most, we invite you to grow with us.

JOB SUMMARY:

This role owns our Maximum Allowable Cost (MAC) and under reimbursement appeal process: identifying claims reimbursed below acquisition cost, building supporting documentation, and submitting timely appeals to PBMs to recover fair payment. This position requires sharp attention to detail, strong recordkeeping discipline, and confident, professional communication with PBM auditors and provider relations teams.

DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

MAC Appeals & Reimbursement Recovery

  • Monitor claims adjudication data to identify claims reimbursed below the pharmacy's acquisition cost or NADAC due to Maximum Allowable Cost (MAC) pricing.
  • Compile MAC appeal packages, including current wholesaler invoices, NDCs, and evidence of drug unavailability at the listed MAC price.
  • Submit timely, well-documented MAC appeals to PBMs in accordance with each payer's required format and appeal window.
  • Track the status of all submitted appeals, follow up on outstanding requests, and escalate denied or unresolved appeals as needed.
  • Analyze appeal outcomes and reimbursement trends to flag drugs/NDCs with chronic underpayment issues for ongoing appeal or formulary discussion.
  • Communicate directly with PBM provider relations and pricing teams to resolve disputes and confirm MAC list pricing updates once appeals are substantiated.
  • Report reimbursement recovery results, denial trends, and outstanding audit risk to pharmacy leadership on a regular basis.
  • Assist PBM and payer audit team in the collection of data such as hard-copy prescriptions, signature logs, proof-of-delivery records, wholesaler invoices, and inventory records — within each PBM's mandated turnaround time.
  • Stay current on each PBM's provider manual, network agreement terms, and audit appeal procedures and deadlines.

Zo werkt het

Het echte werk begint al bij de start van jouw carrière bij Beter Horen. Wij geloven dat je het meeste leert door te doen. Jij mag dus meteen aan de slag in een Beter Horen winkel in jouw regio.

Ondertussen brengen onze coaches je tijdens de opleidingsdagen aan onze eigen Beter Horen Academy de belangrijkste kennis en skills op het gebied van het gehoor, hooroplossingen en adviserend verkopen bij. Je maakt kennis met de nieuwste technieken in de wereld van de audiologie en leert hoe je commerciële kansen optimaal kunt benutten. Je zult al snel ervaren dat het vak van Audicien de ideale combinatie is tussen service, sales en techniek.

Na deze interne opleiding start je aan de audiciensopleiding, waarbij wij samenwerken met het Deltion College in Zwolle en/of Dutch HealthTec Academy in Utrecht (DHTA)We maken gebruik van de nieuwste innovatieve manieren van werkplekleren. Dat wil zeggen dat je het meeste online en in de praktijk leert en dus minder klassikale bijeenkomsten hoeft bij te wonen.

Na twee jaar hard werken word jij beloond met een erkend mbo-4 diploma en mag jij jezelf officieel Audicien noemen. Klinkt goed toch?

Hoe ziet jouw dag eruit?

title: DRM Software Engineer
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) Commerce group is looking for an extraordinary DRM Software Engineer that will help protect the experiences that hundreds of millions of people trust every day—from Apple TV and Apple Music to Fitness+, Podcasts, and Apple Books. Here, security isn't just a feature; it's the foundation that lets creativity and commerce thrive at an unprecedented scale. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge DRM technologies—FairPlay, PlayReady, and Widevine—and the endpoint security systems that safeguard our entire ecosystem, from device signatures to user tokens. This is a team that doesn't just maintain what exists; it questions assumptions, explores gray areas, and builds the next generation of security infrastructure from the ground up. Whether you're a seasoned engineer or someone eager to grow into this space, you'll be empowered to drive projects from idea to production, obsess over performance and scale, and collaborate with some of the best engineers in the industry. If you're energized by big challenges and want your work to protect and power extraordinary experiences for millions of customers, this is where you belong.

At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job, and there's no telling what you could accomplish. As a DRM Software Engineer within the Apple Media Products Commerce team, you will have the opportunity to develop and implement DRM and security solutions across our entire ecosystem of media products. We strive to provide a flawless experience for our millions of customers and developers. The Apple Media Products Commerce Engineering team manages DRM and media security solutions across all Apple media products, including Apple TV, Apple Music, Fitness+, Podcasts, Apple Books, and more. Beyond media playback, our team is responsible for the security of the entire organization's endpoints. We utilize FairPlay technology to verify device signatures, manage device one-time passwords, and ensure the absolute security of user tokens. This scale is truly unprecedented and requires tremendous thinking to develop new initiatives and maintain existing systems. We are looking for a self-starting, energetic individual who is not afraid to question assumptions or charge head-first into gray areas. While prior experience isn't strictly required, an ideal candidate will have, or be eager to develop, an interest in DRM technologies, including FairPlay, PlayReady, and Widevine, as well as endpoint security and authentication protocols. An understanding of relational databases, data-modeling techniques, and Cassandra or other NoSQL knowledge is a plus. We are primarily a Java shop. You will drive projects from inception to production deployment with a strong focus on performance to get the most out of your systems' designs and implementations, no matter what the scale. You will care about measuring, profiling, and tuning, but you will also be able to think creatively and question assumptions. You should be a phenomenal teammate and have excellent communication and presentation skills. If you like the stimulation and challenges of building systems and features exposed to hundreds of millions of transacting users, and you want to make a difference, you will find Apple Media Products Engineering to be a fast-paced, rewarding environment where the best engineers and scientists collaborate to deliver fantastic products and features to our customers.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2+ years experience in software development.
  • Interest in (or willingness to develop expertise in) DRM technologies such as FairPlay, PlayReady, or Widevine
  • Interest in endpoint security and authentication protocols
  • Strong programming skills, primarily in Java
  • Ability to drive projects independently, from inception to production deployment
  • Strong focus on performance — comfortable measuring, profiling, and tuning systems
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills
  • A self-starting, energetic mindset — comfortable questioning assumptions and navigating ambiguity ("gray areas")
  • Strong collaborative instincts
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior hands-on experience with DRM technologies (FairPlay, PlayReady, Widevine)
  • Understanding of relational databases and data-modeling techniques
  • Familiarity with Cassandra or other NoSQL databases

Position Summary:

This position utilizes their lived experience combined with formal training to instill hope, inspire change, and support other individuals through similar experiences, using personal connection, person centered care, and their shared understanding to navigate their life in recovery. A Certified Peer Support Professional provides a wide variety of services to clients and families to ensure compliance with scheduled follow-up appointments with medical providers. This position operates under minimal supervision and must exercise tact, judgment, and confidentiality in contact with the public, clients, and families, as well as fellow associates of the Center. The work is very broad in scope and requires a high level of professionalism.

Position Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Demonstrate the ability to complete client assessments, evaluate a client’s ability to perform daily living activities and independent living skills, identify presenting problem(s), history, medical information, family involvement, psychosocial/psychosexual information, and other pertinent information to form an appropriate clinical impression including substance use/abuse and abuse/neglect.
  • Demonstrate a basic understanding of treatment plans and service lines in which client has been referred to within the Center.
  • Document timely, accurately and in accordance with Center policies utilizing current systems and practices.
  • Document accurate information, which reflects client progress based on the appropriate therapeutic modality. Therapeutic services will be time limited and specific to the presenting problem(s) of each assigned client
  • Provide input as to the client’s progress towards treatment plan goals and objectives, communicating pertinent information regularly with the primary case manager so such information can be presented at staffing.

title: Medical Laboratory Scientist
description:
HealthPartners is hiring for a Medical Laboratory Scientist to help support the Central lab

QUALIFICATIONS:

REQUIRED:

Bachelor of Science degree in Medical Technology or a related science from an accredited college or university and subsequent to graduation, have at least 12 months of appropriate clinical education and 2 years previous experience in a specified area. OR Two-year Associate Decree, appropriate clinical education and HEW certification as a Medical Technologist plus 5 years experience in a specified area.

Certified as Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) by National Certification Agency (NCA) and/or Medical Technologist (MT) by American Society of Clinical Pathologists (ASCP).

Additional skills necessary: good oral and written communication, basic leadership capabilities and good organizational skills.

POSITION PURPOSE:

Service excellence is to be centered on patient care and patient relationships and is the responsibility of all employees. Teamwork is the norm and all employees will be held accountable to work as effective team members. This individual performs a variety of laboratory tests, assists the Lead Medical Technologist with establishing and implementing new lab procedures/instrumentation and serves as a reference for other laboratory personnel as authorized by the Laboratory Supervisor.

ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Support and conform to laboratory safety policies. Know fire and disaster plans as pertaining to the laboratory. Recognize potential chemical and biological hazards and handles these materials as per established protocol.
  • Knowledgeable in specimen requirements and proper handling of specimen prior to testing. Have an understanding of existing policies for specimen identification and criteria for specimen rejection.
  • Perform a variety of tests according to established procedure and performance qualifications established by laboratory management. Will be responsible for having theoretical knowledge of test reactions, knowing expected patient values and any factors causing false reactions.
  • Have understanding of Group Health protocol for quality control. Help Lead Medical Technologist to ensure that the established protocol for quality control is being done and within accepted limits and capable of individually implementing corrective action when indicated.
  • Manifest technical competence in designated area and act as a resource person for the laboratory personnel, nursing personnel and physicians. May be called upon to present technical information to other laboratory personnel and be required to discuss test results with providers.
  • Must be able to make sound independent decisions regarding troubleshooting and corrective actions whenever control or patient rest results fall outside expected performance limits.
  • Ensure that established protocol for equipment maintenance and instrument calibration is performed on a regular basis. Recognize instrument malfunctions. Capable of troubleshooting instrument malfunction by performing repairs in-house if possible or identify the need for external service.
  • Have a working knowledge of database of laboratory computer system. Must be capable of performing designated functions in the computer system.
  • Assist in evaluating new products and instrumentation upon direction of laboratory Supervisor and/or Lead Medical Technologists.
  • Assist Lead Medical Technologist in verifying the accuracy of all work performed within the department. Must be capable of assuming the Lead Medical Technologist duties for short periods of time during the Lead Medical Technologist’s vacations or leaves of absence.
  • Maintain an on-going awareness of current technical information related to designated area of responsibility.
  • Assist in the teaching of laboratory technician students. This teaching includes the theory of the test reactions as well as practical laboratory techniques.
  • Perform other laboratory-related work as assigned by the Laboratory Supervisor and/or Lead Medical Technologist.

title: Supply Distribution Technician - Chambersburg Hospital - Day
description:
Position Function: Under the supervision and/or direction of the Supply Distribution Manager or designee, processes and distributes all consumable medical supplies and equipment throughout the Chambersburg Hospital.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities
Unit Based Essential Functions and Responsibilities



Job Class Specifics
1. Utilizes proper body mechanics to prevent injury to self and others.
2. Performs all work in accordance with organizational and departmental policies and procedures.
3. Independently completes all duties and performs them accurately, recognizing their importance and relationship to patient care.
4. Assists in establishing Performance Improvement Program for department.
5. Seeks assistance from Supervisor/Manager with problems outside the scope of responsibilities.
6. Maintains knowledge of current trends, issues and practices in healthcare Supply Chain and Inventory Control.
7. Participates in cross-training, seminars and in-services as made available for job improvement opportunities.
8. Ensures supply transactions are accurately documented and entered into Supply Chain computer system as they occur.
9. Processes and reviews inventory auto-replenishment program required to initiate requisitions and ensure appropriate levels of inventory are maintained.
10. Performs scheduled inventory counts for assigned par level locations in accordance with replenishment schedule.
11. Picks supplies and restocks par locations.
12. Prioritizes workload to ensure that replenishment schedule is followed.
13. Picks supplies based on OR schedule, requisitions and/or pick tickets.
14. Provides direct delivery replenishment services to departments with no par level inventory.
15. Receives and processes transfers from other Summit warehouses and direct vendor deliveries.
16. Receives implants and other OR case-specific deliveries.
17. Ensures accurate and on-time deliveries to all customers.
18. Reports problems, delays and supply concerns to management in a timely manner.
19. Assists with new employee orientation.


General Requirements

The following requirements are expected of all employees:

Core Values: Integrity, Compassion, Excellence, Service
Annual Health Screening with Infection Control and Blood Borne Pathogens Education
Safety Awareness: Hospital Fire, Safety, and Disaster procedures
Confidentiality: Maintains employee and patient confidentiality.
Attendance: Regular attendance is an essential function of the position
Leadership Standards:
Character: Attitude, Integrity, Role Modeling
Job Performance: Results orientation, Customer focus, Decision making, Awareness
Interpersonal Skills: Communication, Relationship-building, Team player, Celebration
Innovation: Breakthrough Thinking, Knowledge-Building/Sharing, Coaching/Empowering, System Vision & Management

Physical and Mental Requirements: Classified as heavy work by the Dictionary of Occupational Titles:
• Will exert 50 to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or 30 to 60 pounds of force frequently, and/or 25 to 35 pounds of force constantly in order to move objects.
• Frequently reaches overhead to pull or place supplies. May also need to climb on a step-stool to reach some items.
• Frequently bends and squats from an upright position to lower levels.
• Constantly reaches from side to side.
• Twists from the waist on a frequent basis.
• Ability to operate hand/arm controls in order to manipulate supplies and equipment.
• Ability to move rapidly to perform duties to prevent nurse and physician downtime (particularly during emergencies which may occur during tour of duty).
• Near-visual acuity necessary for deciphering fine print, viewing computer screen, and distinguishing sizes and shapes.
• Auditory acuity adequate for hearing normal voice tones when not facing the individual and/or when muffled through a face mask, telephone conversation, intercom, overhead pagers, fire alarms, etc.
• Ability to constantly anticipate and respond to changes in workload schedule/procedures and establish priorities accordingly.
• Lifts up to 45 pounds from waist level to floor and vice versa on a constant basis.
• Carries up to 35 pounds frequently for distances of up to 100 feet.
• Pushes/pulls up to 400 pounds frequently on wheeled carts during each shift in order to access and move/transport supplies and equipment.
Mental requirements:
• Possesses good general mental health.
• Works well under pressure while relating to hospital staff.
• Able to read, speak and write the English language.
• Verbal ability for communicating constantly and effectively with team members.
• Ability to read, write and comprehend medical terminology; simple arithmetic skills necessary in order to pick, receive and restock supplies.
• Ability to maintain positive attitude while serving customers and interacting with other employees.

Working Environment: Stands and walks constantly on tile, concrete and carpeted flooring. Walks throughout the entire hospital complex. Sits occasionally on hard or cushioned chair. Work is performed in a fast-paced, high demand, indoor environment; requires standing and walking for long periods of time without interuption; exposure to clean and sterile environments and patient care units. Work requires flexibility in scheduling.

Reporting Structure: Reports to Supply Distribution Manager. In his/her absence reports to the Vice President for Supply Chain.

Disclaimer: These essential job functions are requirements of the position, which must be performed either with or without reasonable accommodation. The essential job function list is intended to be a guide rather than a limitation. The Chambersburg Hospital possesses the right to add new responsibilities to the list as business demands dictate. Some of the essential job functions may exclude individuals who pose a direct threat/significant risk to the health and safety of themselves or others.
By identifying essential job functions, we are in no way stating or implying that these required tasks are the only activities that are to be performed by the employee occupying this position. In addition, employees will also be expected to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties that are included in the job description. The preceding requirements represent only the minimum acceptable levels of knowledge, skills, and/or abilities that a job incumbent must possess; in order to perform the job successfully, the incumbent will possess additional aptitudes so as to perform the other duties that the job description entails.

Qualifications and Standards

Education: High school graduate or equivalent required.

Experience: Experience applying customer service behaviors and communication skills required. Must have at least one (1) or more years of verifiable material handling experience within the last five-year period that includes computerized inventory control methods and applications, and Low Unit of Measure (LUOM) distribution experience or at least (6) months of direct Healthcare Supply Chain experience. Familiarity with bar coding technology and handheld computer devices is preferred. Basic knowledge and understanding of personal computers, keyboarding skills, and common office application software, i.e.: Excel, Word, etc. is required.

Certifications/Licensure: None required.

Person in this position will be responsible for the delivery of clinical substance abuse treatment to clients participating in the program. Essential job functions include those listed below.

title: Director of the Enrique V. Del Riego Institute of Trade and Logistics Management
description:
Director, The Enrique V. Del Riego Institute of Trade and Logistics Management

Gus Machado College of Business | St. Thomas University | Miami Gardens, Florida

St. Thomas University (STU) invites applications for the position of Director of the Enrique V. Del Riego Institute of Trade and Logistics Management, a full-time faculty appointment with administrative leadership responsibilities for the institute.

STU seeks an innovative, industry-engaged, and student-centered faculty leader with expertise in Supply Chain Management, Logistics Management, International Trade, and related areas.

The successful candidate will provide academic and strategic leadership for the Institute while teaching, mentoring students, advancing applied research, strengthening industry partnerships, and overseeing the implementation and stewardship of grants and donor-supported initiatives.

The position offers an opportunity to shape the continued development of a multidisciplinary academic and workforce platform connecting business education, supply chain, logistics, international trade, accounting, finance, technology, research, and industry engagement.

The Opportunity

The Director will lead the continued development and growth of the Enrique V. Del Riego Institute of Trade and Logistics Management as a distinctive academic, workforce-development, research, and industry-engagement initiative at St. Thomas University.

The Director will be expected to connect academic excellence with hands-on learning and industry practice, creating meaningful opportunities for students while strengthening the Institute's relationships with employers, government agencies, professional organizations, donors, and community partners.

A significant component of the position will involve ensuring that grant-funded and donor-supported initiatives are successfully implemented and that their impact is clearly documented and communicated.

Essential Responsibilities

The Director will:

  • Provide academic, strategic, and programmatic leadership for the Enrique V. Del Riego Institute of Trade and Logistics Management.
  • Teach courses in Supply Chain Management, Logistics Management, International Trade, and/or related areas.
  • Deliver instruction through lectures, hands-on learning, applied exercises, projects, simulations, and other experiential approaches. These expectations build directly on STU's existing faculty model for this academic area.
  • Mentor undergraduate and graduate students and supervise research, capstone, and applied projects.
  • Maintain scholarly, applied research, professional, and service activities appropriate to the faculty appointment.
  • Lead and assist curriculum development, program enhancement, and continuous improvement of academic, certificate, credential, and workforce offerings.
  • Strengthen interdisciplinary connections among Supply Chain, Logistics Management, International Trade, Business, Accounting, Finance, technology, and related disciplines.
  • Build and sustain relationships with employers, logistics and transportation organizations, ports, airports, import/export organizations, government agencies, professional associations, and other industry partners.
  • Expand internships, apprenticeships, experiential learning, applied research, professional certifications, and employment pathways for students.
  • Oversee the programmatic implementation and stewardship of grants, sponsored projects, philanthropic gifts, and donor-supported initiatives.
  • Monitor grant and project milestones, deliverables, outcomes, and impact.
  • Collaborate with university Philanthropy Office, sponsored programs, Finance, Institutional Research, and other University offices to support effective implementation and accountability.
  • Prepare and contribute to grant reports, donor stewardship reports, impact reports, presentations, and other documentation demonstrating measurable results.
  • Identify opportunities for external funding, industry partnerships, applied research, workforce initiatives, and program growth.
  • Represent the Institute and St. Thomas University with industry, academic, governmental, donor, and community stakeholders.
  • Foster interdisciplinary collaborations and partnerships to showcase the Enrique V. Del Riego Institute of Trade and Logistics Management.

Academic Focus

Candidates with expertise or professional experience in one or more of the following areas are particularly encouraged:

  • Supply Chain Management
  • Logistics Management
  • International Trade
  • Supply Chain Analytics
  • Logistics and Operations Management
  • Green and Sustainable Supply Chains
  • Transportation and Distribution
  • Aviation Logistics
  • Maritime Logistics

  • Import/Export Operations
  • Customs and Trade Compliance
  • International Finance and Trade Finance
  • Digital Supply Chains

  • Supply Chain Risk and Resilience

This position is accountable for performing clinical laboratory testing, following all applicable policies and procedures.

  • Independently performs moderate to highly complex clinical tests following the required procedures and policies. Performs newly introduced tests to the laboratory that require defined skills.
  • Prepares and oversees the preparation of reagents or media as well as stock solutions, standards, and controls. Tests new reagents or controls and evaluates their usefulness based on standard criteria.
  • Determines the acceptability of specimens for testing according to established criteria in testing procedures.
  • Determines calculated results utilizing testing data by means of manual or computerized procedures.
  • Accurately enters results of testing. Checks the computer review reports to monitor accurate reporting of laboratory results. Adheres to analytical schedules to maintain turnaround times of results.
  • Evaluates the acceptability of routine and complex analyses prior to releasing patient reports. Recognizes and takes appropriate action in response to critical values or unusual or unexpected results, and documents action taken.
  • Responsible for preventative maintenance, troubleshooting and calibration of laboratory equipment.
  • Evaluates the results of instrument performance checks. Performs linearity, accuracy and precision checks as required.
  • Performs Quality Control and calibrations with the appropriate frequency and evaluates results, to determine acceptability of result release.
  • Selects and evaluates control materials using established criteria. Initiates a corrective action process whenever test systems do not perform according to the established criteria.
  • Accurately performs and records proficiency testing.
  • Demonstrates the ability to detect and correct technical and operational problems. Notifies the supervisor, and contacts manufacturer or field service support for additional assistance, if necessary.
  • Ensures accurate tracking and labeling of reagents and supplies.
  • Consistently maintains a safe and neat work area.
  • Demonstrates effective two-way communication with staff, immediate manager, suppliers, internal and external customers, via meetings, written and verbal interactions, to create an informed positive environment.
  • Actively participates in staff meetings, and in Quality Improvement meetings as assigned.
  • Takes on additional business-related responsibilities or projects, as delegated by the Supervisor or Manager. This may include but not be limited to evaluation of new techniques and procedures in terms of personnel and requirements, method comparison, cost analysis, establishment of reference ranges, writing and revising technical procedures, and evaluation of productivity and key results measures.
  • Responsible for following all required procedures, practices and related guidelines as provided in company policy and associated procedures for safety, environmental, and infection control.
  • Collects and dispose of waste in proper receptacles.
  • Demonstrates a high level of integrity and honesty in maintaining confidentiality.
  • Provides direct and constant supervision to unlicensed staff as necessary and trains staff in proper performance of both routine and complex procedures. Supports Training Programs, where applicable.
  • Maintains professional growth and development through continuing education. The continuing education must meet the education requirements for California state licensure.
  • Answers phones, transfers, or takes accurate messages.
  • Complies with all health and safety policies, procedures, and practices. Required to use personal protective equipment.
  • Other duties as assigned. This is not an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities, but rather a general description of work performed by the position.

"

title: Assistant Director, Career Management: Supply Chain Management - UTK
description:
This role serves as a strategic part of the Supply Chain Management Career Team through developing and supporting programs and opportunities for SCM students to grow into successful professionals. Situated in the Global Supply Chain Institute within the Haslam College of Business, this position reports to the Director of SCM Student Development and Career Management. The individual in this role will focus a majority of their time supporting graduate students and a portion of their time working with undergraduate SCM programs. This position serves as the primary career coach for students in all MSSCM programs. This role assists students to reach their professional potential by counseling one-on-one, providing resources, and facilitating programs that will ensure career success for students both during their program and beyond. The Assistant Director supports students through 1:1 coaching geared toward experienced professionals, facilitates professional development workshops, and interfaces with students and employers to increase access to job opportunities. Additionally, this role supports undergraduate seniors in career coaching and advances professional development through developing and maintaining career programming that is accessible to all students in the major. The individual in this role also contributes to the growth and success of the supply chain community at UT through helping foster and maintain strong employer partnerships. This role contributes strategically to college and university deliverables of key performance indicators for increased rankings by providing professional development assistance to students that improve their chances of securing roles with top companies and further contributing to our #1 ranked graduate SCM program.

Graduate Student Career Coaching, Resource Development, and Program Execution

  • Serve as the primary liaison to all SCM masters students seeking professional development assistance meeting with 80+ students per semester to discuss career development and assist them in their job search.
  • Consult with graduate students on individualized professional development strategies based on personal career path and goals aiming for 90+% career placement 6-months from graduation.
  • Conduct annual needs assessments, and create, implement, and facilitate virtual programming for MS program based on student and employer feedback
  • Develop tools for tracking and reporting student outcomes for Graduate Business Programs with the goal of ensuring quality career placement in post-graduation outcomes
  • Partner with graduate student staff to facilitate programming at bi-annual Immersion Week for MS SCM Online students, specifically leading all networking and professional development activities for the immersion such as negotiation, elevator pitch, career growth, etc.
  • Facilitate Grad Student networking opportunities at bi-annual Supply Chain Forum and throughout the year in smaller virtual settings
  • In consultation with program directors, develop and implement career curriculum and lessons to MSSCM students throughout the duration of each program.
  • Design and teach a career development weekly seminar for master’s students focused on building the skills, competencies, and professional readiness needed for success in the global supply chain field.
  • Manage content and strategy for MS SCM LinkedIn group
  • Develop targeted graduate recruiting opportunities such as panels, mock-interviews, workshops, and lunch and learns

Undergraduate Program Facilitation, Execution, and Support

  • Evaluate career coaching resources and programming and develop plans for continuous improvement to ensure students are receiving quality support.
  • Co-lead SCM Summer Camp which is a week-long immersive experience for high school students to learn about and engage in the field of Supply Chain Management
  • Coordinate and deliver department-wide career programming from ideation to post-program assessment including develop new programming, identifying and inviting corporate partners to participate, managing event execution and communication, and creating and evaluating program assessment. Programs include resume workshops, mock interview sessions, career exploration events, etc. open to all SCM students geared toward improving chances of securing internships with top companies
  • Gather and assess program data and create reports and make actionable recommendations to department leadership for updates intended to increase SCM undergraduate student engagement to 50% participation per year.
  • Contribute to strategic planning, ideation, communication, logistics, problem-solving, and execution of events consistent with the Supply Chain Management Department and Global Supply Chain Institute’s mission, including career fairs, forums, honors events, drop-in hours, workshops, etc.
  • As needed, mentor and support student groups pertaining to the SCM major
  • Supervise multiple student workers and set weekly, monthly, and annual goals aimed to support other department initiatives

Employer relations and Events

  • Engage with corporate partners at events (such as fairs, forums, conferences, etc.) with the intention of cultivating long-term recruiting relationships that result in companies coming to campus multiple times a year and hiring interns and full-time students.

title: Project Manager – Medical Operations
description:
Project Manager – Medical Operations

Seeking Project Manager – Medical Operations for U.S. Government Support – Iraq (Baghdad & Erbil)

Cherokee Federal is recruiting experienced Project Manager – Medical Operations to support U.S. government medical operations in Iraq. Provide medical-surgical, general, emergency, and specialty nursing support at the Diplomatic Support Hospital or Consulate General Erbil Health Unit. If you’re ready to serve those who serve, we want to hear from you.

The Project Manager – Medical Operations provides overall leadership, oversight, coordination, and accountability for medical-support operations supporting Mission Iraq. The PM ensures appropriate staffing, credentialing, readiness, quality, reporting, medical operations, regulatory compliance, and coordination with PMO and Department of State stakeholders.

This position requires a leader with a strong medical or healthcare operations background who understands clinical operations sufficiently to oversee a multidisciplinary workforce supporting emergency medicine, surgery, nursing, laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, behavioral health, public health, EMS, medical evacuation, and other medical services.

** This role Is contingent upon award.

** Secret Clearance Is Preferred Or ability to obtain required clearance for the role

** Per contract, candidate required to work more than 10 hours as regular shift / Overtime hours / holidays and weekends

Compensation & Benefits:

Estimated Starting Salary Range for Project Manager – Medical Operations: Pay commensurate with experience.

Full-time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K, and other possible benefits as provided. Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.

Responsibilities Include:

  • Provide overall program leadership and operational oversight for medical-support services at Baghdad and Erbil.

  • Ensure continuous staffing and operational readiness of the Diplomatic Support Hospital and Health Unit.

  • Oversee physicians, nurses, paramedics, laboratories, radiology, pharmacy, behavioral health, public health, surgical and other medical-support personnel.

  • Ensure all personnel meet required education, experience, licensing, certification, credentialing, medical-clearance and security-vetting requirements before deployment. This role requires Nomination Packets to contain resumes, credential verification, licenses and required certifications.

  • Maintain adequate staffing levels and develop qualified replacement pipelines for key personnel.

  • Immediately manage staffing gaps, emergency vacancies and backfill requirements; coordinate interim coverage and permanent replacements.

  • Ensure planned R&R and other absences do not negatively affect required medical coverage.

  • Maintain daily personnel accountability and provide staffing status to the customer.

  • Coordinate medical operational priorities with PMO, DOS representatives, medical leadership and other contractors.

  • Ensure medical services support primary, urgent, emergency, trauma, surgical, critical-care and stabilization requirements.

  • Provide operational oversight of medical evacuation procedures and ensure appropriate escalation of mission-impacting patient events.

  • Ensure compliance with FAM, FAH, FAR, DOSAR, USG regulations, Embassy procedures, COM requirements and applicable industry standards.

  • Oversee personnel records, credential expiration tracking, medical clearances, training records and licensing documentation.

  • Protect PII and HIPAA-controlled medical/personnel information.

  • Oversee incident and serious-incident reporting and ensure required notifications are completed within contractual timelines.

  • Ensure patient movements, medical evacuations, mission-impacting cases and serious medical events are escalated appropriately.

  • Lead implementation and maintenance of the program Quality Management System.

  • Monitor performance, corrective actions, compliance, quality inspections and operational improvement initiatives.

  • Ensure completion of daily, monthly, quarterly and ad-hoc contractual reporting, including personnel accountability, operations reports, SitReps, ER/EMS logs, credentials, medical-clearance status, quality reports and other required deliverables.

  • Support transition, mobilization, demobilization, medical readiness and contingency planning.

  • Perform other related program-management responsibilities as required.

Experience, Education, Skills, Abilities requested:

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, Nursing, Public Health, Emergency Medical Services, Health Sciences, Business Administration, Program Management or related field.

  • Minimum 5 years of healthcare/medical operations experience, with at least 3 years in program, project, clinical operations or healthcare management.

  • Experience managing multidisciplinary healthcare personnel.

  • Experience with staffing, clinical credentialing, personnel readiness and healthcare compliance.

  • Experience in managing operational reporting, quality assurance and performance requirements.

  • Demonstrated understanding of emergency/acute-care medical operations.

  • Must have at least three years of experience in their respective labor categories and possess the qualifications, certifications and aptitude necessary for their position.

  • Fluent written and spoken English.

  • Ability to deploy and work in an austere/high-threat environment.

Required Certifications:

  • Current BLS certification is strongly recommended for medically trained candidates.

  • Must be able to satisfy applicable USG security-vetting/MRPT requirements.

  • Must meet applicable pre-deployment medical/fit-for-duty requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in healthcare administration, Public Health, Nursing, Emergency Management, Business Administration or related field.

  • 7–10+ years of healthcare operations experience.

  • Previous OCONUS, Iraq or Middle East region, Department of State, DoW, Embassy or government-contract medical operations experience.

  • Experience managing a hospital, trauma center, emergency department, deployed medical facility or remote-site healthcare program.

  • Experience with medical evacuation, MASCAL/emergency preparedness and deployed clinical staffing.

  • Experience managing subcontractor or federal contract deliverables.

Preferred Certifications:

  • PMP

  • Lean Six Sigma

  • CPHQ

  • ACLS

  • Clinical licenses such as RN, Paramedic, PA/NP or other healthcare professional credentials are highly desirable.

  • Must pass pre-employment requirements of Cherokee Federal.

As a trusted partner for more than 60 federal clients, Cherokee Federal LLCs are focused on building a brighter future, solving complex challenges, and serving the government’s mission with compassion and heart. title: Senior Data Engineer (Databricks)
description:

BU/Segment: Analytics / Data Management / Insurance Domain

Location: London, United Kingdom (Hybrid, 3-4 days in the office)

Employment Type: Permanent to start ASAP

Summary of the role:

We’re looking for a highly skilled Azure Databricks Data Engineer to design, develop and deliver cloud-based data integration and analytics solutions within our Insurance portfolio.

You’ll work across data engineering, modelling, and transformation initiatives — building scalable pipelines, optimising performance, and ensuring best practices in data quality and governance. This is a hands-on technical role requiring strong Azure and Databricks experience, coupled with solid Insurance domain knowledge.

As part of this role, you’ll have the opportunity to work on high-impact Insurance data transformation programmes, collaborating with experienced data professionals in a forward-thinking, innovative environment. You’ll gain exposure to cutting-edge Azure and Databricks technologies.

As part of your duties, you will be responsible for:

  • Design, build, and deploy scalable data pipelines using Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, and Azure SQL Database.
  • Optimise Databricks environments for performance, cost, and security.
  • Develop and maintain data integration, ETL/ELT processes, and data quality frameworks.
  • Translate business requirements into data models, ensuring consistency and accuracy across data layers.
  • Work with stakeholders to deliver effective data solutions, analytics.
  • Create technical documentation including data flow diagrams, architecture design, and test plans.
  • Stay current with emerging data engineering and Azure ecosystem technologies to drive continuous improvement.

Qualifications and experience we consider to be essential for the role:

  • Insurance industry experience is essential, with a strong understanding of policy, claims, and regulatory data.

  • Minimum of 5 years’ management experience required – leading technical delivery or overseeing project teams within data engineering or integration environments.

  • 8–10 years’ experience in data engineering and integration, ideally in enterprise-scale environments.

  • Deep expertise in Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse, and Azure Data Lake.

  • Hands-on experience with Spark (PySpark/SparkSQL), ETL/ELT design, and data pipeline orchestration.

  • Strong data modelling skills (Dimensional, ODS, Data Vault) and experience with data warehousing concepts.

  • Experience working with large, complex datasets and distributed computing environments.

  • Proficiency in SQL, version control (e.g. Git), and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Familiarity with Agile delivery and DevOps practices (Azure DevOps, JIRA, etc.).

Preferred Skills & Experience:

  • Knowledge of EDM (Enterprise Data Management) practices, data governance, metadata management, and lineage tools.

  • Exposure to multi-cloud environments (AWS or GCP).
  • Understanding of modern data architecture philosophies (Dimensional, ODS, Data Vault) and real-time cloud data capabilities.

As part of a leading global analytics and AI solutions company, you can look forward to:

  • A competitive salary with a generous bonus, private healthcare, critical illness life assurance at 4 x your annual salary, income protection insurance, and a rewarding pension.

  • At EXL, we are committed to providing our employees with the tools and resources they need to succeed and excel in their careers. We offer a wide range of professional and personal development opportunities. We also support a range of learning initiatives that allow our employees to build on their existing skills and knowledge. From online courses to seminars and workshops, our employees have the opportunity to enhance their skills and stay up to date with the latest trends and technologies.
  • As an Equal Opportunity Employer, EXL is committed to diversity. Our company does not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, age, or disability status.

title: Semantic Modeler
description:
Location: Montréal,Québec,Canada

About the Role

What if your users could simply ask? We’re building TSIQ, an AI-powered analytics and intelligence platform that answers questions, recommends actions, and runs workflows for the people who use TS Imagine’s Trading, Risk and Prime Brokerage products. As a Semantic Modeler you’ll build both the foundation and the intelligence on top of it—the data models, pipelines, and semantic layers that make our data trustworthy, and the AI agents that turn it into answers. You'll be part of our dynamic Data & Analytics Office, a globally distributed, high-impact team that processes trillions of data points and manages our cutting-edge data lake built on Snowflake.

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of data engineering, semantic modeling, and applied AI—on a product that is being defined as you build it. We have multiple openings across levels, from intermediate through senior.

Why You’ll Love This Role

This position is perfect for:

  • Data Modelers: You believe a great answer starts with a well-designed model, and you take pride in structuring data so others can trust it.
  • Applied AI Builders: You’re fluent in prompt and context engineering, and you’re energized by making AI agents reliable rather than merely impressive.
  • Analytical Minds: You enjoy delving into complex data sets and ensuring the highest quality for accurate decision-making.
  • Problem Framers: You’re comfortable sitting with a business stakeholder, untangling a vague request, and turning it into something buildable.
  • Storytellers: You're comfortable presenting complex data and AI-driven insights in a way that engages and excites stakeholders.
  • Action Takers: You thrive on challenges, taking ownership of a variety of responsibilities to deliver high-quality results.
  • Lifelong Learners: You're always eager to step outside your comfort zone and dive into the intricacies of one of the most complex business domains.
  • Collaborative Teammates: You possess the technical and interpersonal skills to excel in a cutting-edge software development environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and build the data models and pipelines that power TSIQ.
  • Develop semantic models so that AI agents reason over trading, risk, and prime brokerage data with precision and consistency.
  • Build, test, and iterate on AI agents using prompt engineering and context engineering.
  • Implement guardrails, evaluation, and governance controls that keep AI agents accurate, safe, and auditable.
  • Deliver analytics and rapid prototypes in Streamlit to put capabilities in front of users early.
  • Perform business analysis—gather requirements from stakeholders, translate them into technical designs, and validate that what we ship answers the real question.
  • Collaborate with a global team of developers in a fast-paced, innovative setting.

What You Bring

  • Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience with Snowflake.
  • Proficiency in Python, including the ability to contribute to structured, production-grade codebases—not just notebooks.
  • Experience designing data models and building data pipelines, including transformation frameworks such as dbt.
  • Semantic modeling experience—defining metrics, dimensions, and business logic that downstream consumers depend on.
  • Practical prompt engineering and context engineering skills, with a focus on making AI outputs reliable and repeatable.
  • Experience building AI agents and implementing guardrails to govern their behavior (a strong plus).
  • Streamlit or comparable experience building lightweight data applications.
  • Business analysis skills—requirements gathering, stakeholder engagement, and documentation.
  • Exceptional communication skills. This role sits between business stakeholders and the platform, so clear written and verbal communication is essential.
  • Capital markets or financial services domain experience. This is extremely important to us—understanding trading, risk, or prime brokerage workflows will set you apart.

Why Join TS Imagine?

  • On-site role—4 days per week in our Montreal office, with 1 day of flexibility.
  • Unlimited vacation + 3 personal days.
  • Annual bonus and salary review.
  • $1,500 training budget to fuel your growth.
  • RRSP matching (3% company contribution).
  • Comprehensive health insurance.
  • Subsidized public transportation (Opus & Cie).
  • Join a global team with 10 offices worldwide and the opportunity to make a real impact on the financial industry.

Note: This role is not remote—applicants must be based in Montreal.

If you're excited by AI, rigorous about data, and ready to help build something new, we want to hear from you!

description:
Client Services SVP – Private Equity - Luxembourg

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 80 offices worldwide. With more than $2 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

About the Team & Business Line:

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

As a core member of our Fund Accounting team, you will be working with some of the industry’s most accomplished professionals to deliver award-winning services for complex fund structures that our clients can depend upon.

As a Senior Vice President in Client Services, you will be the driving force behind exceptional service delivery for a portfolio of key private equity clients. This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of client partnership, operational leadership, and business growth.

What You'll Be Doing

Client Relationship & Service Excellence

  • Lead and implement a client service programme that sets clear standards and delivers a consistently high-quality experience for key clients
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with C-suite stakeholders and key decision-makers, visiting clients regularly to understand their priorities and evaluate service quality
  • Participate in client calls and oversee reporting delivery, ensuring accuracy and timeliness in line with agreed requirements
  • Act as a senior escalation point for complex client issues, guiding resolution with a calm, solutions-focused approach

Business Development & Growth

  • Identify and pursue new opportunities for growth across the business line
  • Contribute to business development pitches and presentations for both prospective and existing clients

Operational & Risk Oversight

  • Monitor service levels, profitability, and resourcing across the business line, proactively addressing any negative trends
  • Establish and maintain a Risk Management Framework, including quality control reviews and continuous risk assessment of funds under administration
  • Provide monthly reporting on operational risk, key developments, and project status
  • Lead a proactive response to regulatory and industry changes, driving relevant initiatives across Citco Fund Services

People & Team Leadership

  • Manage, develop, and support team members to ensure the effective running of the department
  • Participate in the review of departmental procedures and policies, and support the team in adhering to them
  • Contribute to and lead cross-functional projects as the business continues to grow and evolve

What We're Looking For

  • You are a confident, collaborative leader who brings both strategic thinking and hands-on client focus. You are comfortable engaging at the most senior levels while also supporting your team's day-to-day success. You likely bring:
  • A strong background in financial services, with experience in fund accounting, operations, or product control environments
  • Proven experience leading and developing teams, with a track record of building high-performing, engaged groups
  • The ability to manage complex client relationships with professionalism, empathy, and clarity
  • A sound understanding of risk management principles and how to apply them in a fund services context
  • Excellent communication skills — you can adapt your style whether you're presenting to a client, mentoring a team member, or navigating a complex issue
  • A proactive, growth-oriented mindset with the ability to identify opportunities and act on them

Experience & Skills

  • Degree-level education (bachelor's or master's) or equivalent professional qualification
  • Significant experience in financial services, ideally within fund accounting, operations, or a related discipline
  • Demonstrated experience managing and developing teams at a senior level
  • Familiarity with private equity fund structures is an advantage
  • Strong risk awareness and experience working within governance or compliance frameworks

Ways of Working

In this role, you will operate with a high degree of autonomy while remaining closely connected to clients, colleagues, and senior leadership. You will collaborate across business lines — from operations and technology to compliance and business development — and will be a visible, trusted voice both internally and externally. Decision-making is informed, considered, and client-centred, and you will be empowered to shape how the team works and grows.

Our Benefits

Your well being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection.

description:
General Practitioner

Location: White Cross New Brighton, Christchurch
Hours: 32 Hours Per Week

About the Role

We are seeking a General Practitioner to join our experienced and supportive team at White Cross New Brighton.

This is an opportunity to enjoy a better balance between work and life while delivering high-quality, community-focused healthcare within a well-established and trusted practice. With a consistent four-day work week and minimal weekend commitments, you will have more time to enjoy everything Christchurch and the surrounding Canterbury region have to offer.

Serving a diverse and growing patient population, this role offers the opportunity to build meaningful, long-term relationships with patients and their families while making a genuine difference to community health outcomes. As a frontline healthcare provider, you will play an important role in ensuring patients can access timely primary care, helping to prevent avoidable hospital admissions and reducing pressure on secondary healthcare services.

Supported by experienced nurses, administration teams, and the wider Tamaki Health network, you will have the resources and support needed to focus on delivering exceptional patient care while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

What You Will Do

As a valued member of the clinical team, you will:

  • Deliver high-quality, patient-centred general practice care.
  • Assess, diagnose, and manage acute and long-term health conditions.
  • Develop and maintain meaningful therapeutic relationships with patients and their families.
  • Promote preventative healthcare and support positive health outcomes.
  • Work collaboratively with nursing and multidisciplinary teams to provide coordinated care.
  • Support continuity of care through proactive patient management and follow-up.
  • Contribute to reducing avoidable hospital presentations through accessible community-based healthcare.
  • Maintain accurate clinical records and documentation in accordance with professional standards.

What You Will Bring

To be successful in this role, you will have:

  • Registration with the Medical Council of New Zealand and a current Annual Practising Certificate, or eligibility for registration.
  • Experience working as a General Practitioner within primary care.
  • Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and decision-making skills.
  • A commitment to delivering culturally safe, patient-centred healthcare.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.
  • A collaborative approach and passion for working within multidisciplinary teams.
  • A genuine desire to improve health outcomes within the community.

About White Cross New Brighton

White Cross New Brighton is a well-established practice located within one of Christchurch's most vibrant coastal communities. The clinic has built strong and trusted relationships with local patients and provides comprehensive healthcare services to a diverse patient population.

As part of the Tamaki Health network, you will benefit from the support of one of New Zealand's largest primary healthcare providers, offering access to clinical leadership, operational expertise, and a broader network of healthcare professionals.

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!

Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.

Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly's operational and analytical systems.

This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.

What you will do

  • Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
  • Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
  • Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.
  • Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products.
  • Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution.
  • Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery.
  • Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes.
  • Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations.

What we are looking for

  • Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes.
  • Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance.
  • Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more.
  • Experience building software that other engineers use: CLIs, internal platforms, control planes, automation, CI validation, developer tooling, or self-service workflows.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud or infrastructure platforms, including runtime isolation, deployment, observability, and operational ownership.
  • Ability to turn ambiguous architectural direction into practical increments, make trade-offs explicit, and deliver useful production systems without waiting for perfect certainty.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in English. This role involves aligning multiple engineering teams around standards, contracts, and ownership boundaries.

Useful experience, but not required

  • DataHub or other data catalog, lineage, or governance systems.
  • Open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, object-store-backed data lakes, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse, or analytical storage systems.
  • GitHub Actions, policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, controllers, operators, or reconciliation-based systems.
  • Data contracts, schema registries, Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema, compatibility checking, field-level metadata, or contract testing.
  • Experience supporting analytics, AI/ML, feature-store-style access patterns, or cross-domain product-service integrations.
  • Experience with JVM languages and Python, TypeScript, Go, or Ruby.

What we offer you

At Smartly, we offer a place where you can do meaningful technical work while growing with a global team.

  • Inclusive global culture built on trust, transparency, open feedback, and respect for different perspectives.
  • Global impact through technology used by major brands to plan, create, optimize, and understand digital advertising at scale.
  • Wellbeing support, paid holidays, family leave, and sustainable ways of working.
